newsitem.title: USA: US confirms Continental settlement on Iraqi sales.
newsitem.headline: US confirms Continental settlement on Iraqi sales.

text.p: The U.S. Justice and Agriculture Departments confirmed Monday that a foreign-based affiliate of Continental Grain Co pleaded guilty to conspiring to defraud USDA on sales of agricultural products to Iraq from 1987 through 1990.
The plea agreement required the affiliate, Arab Finagrain Agri-Business Trading Ltd, to pay a $10-million criminal fine, the Justice Department said.
It said Continental, in a related civil settlement, agreed to pay an additional $25 million to resolve the government's civil claims in connection with the investigation.
Continental earlier announced the terms of the settlement.

According to the criminal charges, Arab Finagrain used Continental to register for sales of soybean meal and protein concentrate under USDA's export credit guarantee program because Arab Finagrain -- with no office or presence in the United States -- was ineligible to take part in the program.

USDA Inspector General Roger Viadero said in a statement that Arab Finagrain and certain of its affiliated companies had voluntarily agreed to no longer take part in any U.S. government funded, guaranteed or sponsored programs.
